title: She hid a scarlet cord in her window.
paragraphs:
She hid a scarlet cord in her window.
God hid a Redeemer in her bloodline.
And most people never connect the two.

Because we love the story of Boaz.
We preach about redemption in the fields.
We admire his integrity, his kindness, his power to restore Ruth.
But we skip the woman who raised him.
And here’s the tension you can’t ignore—

How does a woman known for selling her body
raise a man known for restoring dignity?
Because if you miss this, you miss the Gospel buried in the genealogy.
Some of us are living like Rahab before the rope.

Surviving.
Compromising.
Making peace with patterns we know are killing us.

Secret habits.
Private compromises.
Silent addictions.

You smile in public…
but negotiate with darkness in private.
And you’ve started believing the lie:

A woman in Jericho.
A city marked for judgment.
A life shaped by survival.
“I know that the Lord has given you the land…” (Joshua 2:9)

Before the walls fell—
her heart did.
She risked everything on a God she had never seen.

Joshua 2:18
“Bind this line of scarlet cord in the window…”

A visible surrender.
A public alignment.
A line drawn between her old life and God’s mercy.

Some scholars interpret the scarlet cord as a prophetic picture—
a symbol pointing forward to the blood that would one day save completely.
Now here’s where it gets personal.

Joshua 6:25
“But Rahab the prostitute… lives in Israel to this day.”

Matthew 1:5
“Salmon the father of Boaz, whose mother was Rahab…”
The Bible doesn’t hide her past.
Because grace is not embarrassed by your history.
Boaz didn’t grow up in a perfect home.
He grew up in a redeemed one.

“I was lost… but God saw me.”
“I was bound… but God covered me.”
“I was outside… but God brought me in.”
Her past didn’t leak into his life as poison—
it flowed into his life as perspective.
That’s why he didn’t reject her.
Because he had seen grace up close.
You’re afraid your past will damage your future.
You’re afraid your hidden sin will disqualify your calling.
You’re afraid your story will contaminate the people around you.
But Rahab’s life shouts something louder:

What you surrender to God
will not destroy your legacy—
it will define it.

Romans 3:23
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
The secret sin no one claps for.

The pride you justify.
The lust you manage.
The compromise you excuse.
And that’s where the story turns.
Because the same scarlet thread in Rahab’s window…
echoes in a wooden cross outside Jerusalem.
Jesus Christ didn’t come to admire your potential.
He came to carry your sin.

1 Peter 2:24
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…”
All of it placed on Him.

You are more sinful than you admit—
but more loved than you can imagine.
And now offers you what Rahab received—

2 Corinthians 5:17
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation…”

She had to believe.
She had to act.
She had to tie the cord.
but it must be received personally.

You can’t inherit it.
You can’t fake it.
You can’t delay it forever.
So what are you going to do with your scarlet cord?
Or receive a new name in Christ?
Rahab’s decision didn’t just save her.

Your surrender today
can rewrite someone else’s tomorrow.

Turn from sin.
Turn toward Him.
Tie your life to the cross.
And watch God do what only He can do—
